slides.0.title: Level 1 review
slides.0.subtitle: Four questions that tie Morocco together
slides.1.title: Four questions
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Where?
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The northern half, with the Meknès plateau at its core relying on altitude for acidity, and coastal regions moderated by the Atlantic
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Why the rise and fall?
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Planted for export under the French; declined with the 1967 quotas and state control; revived by foreign leases in the 1990s
slides.1.highlights.2.title: What is in the glass?
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Mostly red, with Cinsault and Carignan as tradition and Syrah and Cabernet as modern; vin gris is a distinctive category named in the rules
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Who makes it, and for whom?
slides.1.highlights.3.content: A few large firms plus French capital; mostly domestic sales; retail limited by the 1967 rule
slides.1.content: If you can answer these four in your own words, you are ready for the regulations.
slides.2.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Level 1 assessment
Where are Morocco's vineyards mainly found?
A. Only on the Mediterranean coast
B. Only high in the Atlas
C. The northern half
D. The southern Sahara
From Berkane to Doukkala.
Which is a key condition of the Meknès plateau?
A. Heavy sea fog
B. Rain all year
C. The cool of 50°N
D. The day-night swing from altitude
An inland plateau relies on altitude, not the sea.
Roughly what was wine output in the 1950s?
A. 2–3 million hl a year
B. 30,000 hl a year
C. 30 million hl a year
D. Almost none
Far higher than today.
What was Morocco's first AOC?
A. Doukkala
B. Les Coteaux de l'Atlas
C. Crémant de l'Atlas
D. Les Côtes de Rommani
The order is dated 8 October 1998.
How do the roles of Cinsault and Syrah differ?
A. Syrah is native; Cinsault is international
B. Both are banned by law
C. Cinsault is the traditional base; Syrah grew with the premium revival
D. Cinsault is white; Syrah is red
Both are on the permitted list.
What is the standing of vin gris in Morocco?
A. Banned by law
B. Export only
C. A sweet wine
D. A category named in AOC rules
The Coteaux de l'Atlas order names red, rosé, gris and white.
What does article 28 of the 17 July 1967 decree say?
A. Licensed sellers may not sell alcohol to Moroccan Muslims
B. Wine production is banned
C. Wine exports are banned
D. All vineyards are nationalised
Production is legal; it is sale that is restricted.
Which best sums up the Moroccan wine market?
A. All bought and destroyed by the state
B. Mostly domestic, with a small export share
C. Almost all exported to France
D. Almost all exported to the US
The reverse of the export model of the 1950s.
